notes: דֵּי שֶׂה is split, with for on the construct דֵּי and a lamb on the rectum, so that no lexical noun is left holding an English rendering unaligned (rule 19); the competing reading treating for as the rectum's relational expression is named in that unit's note (rule 8).
The idiom לֹא תִמְצָא יָדָהּ is aligned morpheme by morpheme onto the ASV's recasting — her means suffice not — with the negative discontinuous from its Hebrew position under rule 25.
The two אֶחָד units take the determiners the ASV writes for them (the one, the other) and head on the numeral, which carries the lexeme (rules 15, 31).

תֹרִים → turtle doves heads on doves under rule 31's tie clause, with the competing head on turtle named in that unit's note; the same tie recurs at LEV.12.6 and was decided there on its own evidence.
כִּפֶּר heads on atonement as a light verb plus complement (rule 44), and the explicit subject הַכֹּהֵן takes only its own English (rule 17).
